note: WHAT THE MERGE QUEUE IS ACTUALLY FOR, named by the chamber operator during The Tackle and worth more than the phase list suggests. Its value on a byte-identity campaign was NOT that it ran more tests than the campaign did. It is that it measured THE OBJECT THAT LANDS -- main plus branch, merged -- using an instrument the campaign did not configure, operated by a session that did not know the acceptance criterion until it was told. Both halves matter separately. A local rebaseline runs on the BRANCH TIP, which is not the thing that lands; and a criterion you wrote, checked by a command you chose, on a tree you built, is careful self-measurement rather than independent confirmation. So there are three questions, not two: does the check pass, CAN the check fail (that is what a positive control answers), and who configured it and on which object. The third is the easy one to skip, because passing the first two already feels like rigour. Concretely on The Tackle: local runs said drift-exit=0 on the branch tip; the chamber regenerated every artifact from the MERGED tree and found the type-audit report already correct, moving nothing but its own timing rows. The second result is the one that discharges the criterion, and it is the only evidence in the campaign not downstream of the campaign own instrumentation. Practical form when reporting a green: say WHICH of the three you have, because I verified it locally and the chamber verified it on the merge product are different claims and only the second is independent.
